intended_object: The tensor product f ⊗ g of closed (even, degree-0) morphisms of matrix factorizations f : X → X' (of v) and g : Y → Y' (of w). It is a morphism X ⊗ Y → X' ⊗ Y' of matrix factorizations of v + w and acts componentwise on (X⊗Y)₀ = X₀⊗Y₀ ⊕ X₁⊗Y₁ and (X⊗Y)₁ = X₁⊗Y₀ ⊕ X₀⊗Y₁. I took this from the docstring and the module documentation, which cite Knörrer and Orlov.
explanation:
The definition wraps `CurvedDuplex.tensorHom f.hom g.hom`. That map has even component `biprod.map (f₀ ⊗ g₀) (f₁ ⊗ g₁)` and odd component `biprod.map (f₁ ⊗ g₀) (f₀ ⊗ g₁)`. This is the standard tensor product of even morphisms of Z/2-graded objects, matching the components of `tensorObj`. Within the Lean definition, the `comm₀`/`comm₁` fields prove that the result commutes with the tensor differentials. Downstream, the library proves functoriality (`id_tensorHom_id`, `tensorHom_comp_tensorHom`) and bilinearity, and builds the bifunctor `tensor` from this map.

On generality: the construction is already stated in full generality one level down, as `CurvedDuplex.tensorHom` over a monoidal preadditive linear category. This definition only lifts it to the subcategory of matrix factorizations (finitely generated projective modules over a commutative ring), which is the natural setting for matrix factorizations. Mathlib has no matrix factorizations, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
